entities.summary: King Li of Zhou, personal name Ji Hu, ruled from approximately 877–841 BC or 857–842 BC, making him one of the longest-reigning rulers of the Zhou dynasty. During his reign, Li Li of Zhou oversaw significant territorial expansion, including the conquest of the neighboring state of Jin. He also established a new capital, Feng, which became a major center of trade and culture. Li Li of Zhou is remembered for his military campaigns and his efforts to consolidate power and establish a strong dynasty. His reign marked a significant turning point in the history of ancient China, as he expanded the Zhou dynasty's influence and established a new capital that would become a major cultural and economic center. The legacy of King Li of Zhou can be seen in the continued influence of the Zhou dynasty on Chinese politics, culture, and society, as well as in the many historical records and artifacts that have survived to the present day.
